reference.source: GeneReviews / Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: Named for the vertical iris or chorioretinal coloboma that can give a cat-like pupil, though this is present in only a minority
The classic and variably complete triad is iris coloboma, anal atresia or another anorectal anomaly, and preauricular pits or tags
Caused by a small supernumerary marker chromosome producing partial tetrasomy of proximal 22q, including the cat eye critical region
Congenital heart disease is common, notably total anomalous pulmonary venous return as well as septal and conotruncal defects
Renal malformations such as agenesis, hypoplasia, and dysplasia occur frequently
Intellect is often normal or only mildly impaired, with wide variability
Expressivity is highly variable, so mildly affected relatives may be identified only on testing
Down-slanting palpebral fissures and other subtle facial features may be present
reference.pathophysiology: Cat eye syndrome is caused by a small bisatellited supernumerary marker chromosome derived from the proximal long arm and part of the short arm of chromosome 22, producing partial tetrasomy, or sometimes trisomy, of the cat eye critical region at 22q11. The extra genetic dosage of this region disturbs development of neural crest and other tissues, explaining the ocular colobomata, ear anomalies, and the anorectal, cardiac, and renal malformations. Expressivity is markedly variable, probably reflecting differences in marker content and mosaicism.
additionalDifferentials: CHARGE syndrome, given coloboma, cardiac defects, and ear anomalies
VACTERL association, given anorectal, cardiac, and renal involvement
Townes-Brocks syndrome, given anal, ear, and renal anomalies
additionalInvestigations: Karyotype to detect the small marker chromosome
FISH or microarray to confirm the marker derives from 22q11 and to define copy number
Echocardiography, screening specifically for anomalous pulmonary venous return and other defects
Assessment of anorectal anatomy in the newborn
redFlags: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return or another critical cardiac lesion
Anorectal malformation requiring urgent surgical management
Significant renal malformation with impaired function
reference.prognosis: Very variable; many individuals have normal or near-normal intellect and a good outcome, but prognosis is dominated by the severity of any cardiac and renal malformation.
pitfalls: Expecting the ocular coloboma to be present in every case, when it is not
Missing the small marker chromosome without dedicated FISH or microarray
Overlooking anomalous pulmonary venous return on cardiac screening
Underestimating variability and failing to test at-risk relatives
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
Gardner and Sutherland's Chromosome Abnormalities and Genetic Counseling
management: Surgical correction of congenital heart defects, notably total anomalous pulmonary venous return and septal or conotruncal lesions
Neonatal surgical management of anal atresia and other anorectal anomalies
Assessment and management of renal malformations with monitoring of renal function
Ophthalmological follow-up for iris and chorioretinal coloboma to protect vision
Developmental assessment and educational support given the variable intellectual outcome
Multidisciplinary paediatric care coordinating cardiology, surgery, nephrology and ophthalmology
Genetic counselling, with karyotype and microarray confirmation of the supernumerary marker chromosome
